title: Stream contract: slimline SDK sprint notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick sprint-level working notes that try to compress a usable streaming + tool-call contract into a small SDK surface for first-party clients. Not a final PRD — more of a scoping + tradeoffs dump for the sprint.

Context and problem:
- Teams building incremental UIs (mutating progress bars, progressive answers, editor assistants) want: consistent incremental tokens, typed tool-call events, ability to resume interrupted streams, minimal client surface area.
- Current hosted-api designs try to cover many complex edge cases; this doc experiments with a "slimline" contract: small number of primitives, explicit client responsibilities, server guarantees that enable simple SDKs.

High-level goals:
- Small SDK API (<= 4 public methods) for common flows: startStream(), onDelta(), callTool(), resumeStream().
- Strong incremental framing so SDKs can render partial structured output without re-parsing entire transcript.
- Deterministic tool-call lifecycle: single canonical event per tool invocation, idempotent retries supported.
- Resume token that is tiny (opaque string) and cheap to compute on server.
- Telemetry hooks: token-count, latency-per-chunk, toolcall-latency, errors.

Non-goals for this sprint:
- Full offline-first sync or multi-device session merge.
- Rich session snapshotting beyond resume token and short checkpoint.
- SDKs for every platform (focus: web + Node first).

Proposed primitives (contract):
1) Frames over a streaming socket (WebSocket / HTTP/2 / SSE)
   - Types: {type: "delta" | "tool_event" | "checkpoint" | "resume_ack" | "error"}
   - Delta frame: carries partial text and optional structured-patches (json-schema-lite).
   - Tool_event frame: emits when model requests a tool or when tool result is returned. Canonical ordering: delta frames up to tool request -> tool_event(request) -> (optional) delta pause -> tool_event(response) -> delta resume.
   - Checkpoint frame: lightweight snapshot mapping to resume token.

2) Start request semantics
   - startStream(payload): payload contains prompt, options (max_tokens, model, structured_schema_id, prefer_low_latency boolean). Server returns initial stream id and possibly an initial checkpoint.

3) Resume
   - resumeStream(stream_id, resume_token): server verifies token, responds with resume_ack and continues streaming from that logical point. If token stale or invalid, server returns error with suggested re-run behavior.

4) Tool call lifecycle and idempotency
   - Each callTool() from client synthesizes a client-generated id (cid). Server will reflect that cid in tool_event frames so client can correlate.
   - Tool requests from model include a tool_spec (name, version, schema) and a deterministic signature for same input -> same cid mapping when server-side replays.
   - Retries: client may re-send the same cid to re-associate a prior in-flight call. Server must dedupe by cid for a limited retention window (e.g., 30s).

Structured output approach:
- Avoid forcing a heavy schema at stream start. Instead: optional structured_schema_id points to a lightweight schema (JSON-LD style) that server uses to emit structured-patches inside delta frames.
- Structured patches are three-part: path (json-pointer), op (add/replace/remove), value (string/json). Clients can apply patches incrementally.
- When structured output present, SDK exposes both raw text deltas and structured_patch events so UIs can choose which to render.

SDK ergonomics (web/node focus):
Public surface (target):
- startStream(req): returns StreamHandle (object) with on(event, cb) and close()/cancel().
- Stream events: "delta" (text fragment), "patch" (structured_patch), "tool_request" (tool_spec, cid), "tool_response" (cid, result), "checkpoint" (resume_token), "end", "error".
- callTool(cid, toolPayload): convenience for responding to tool_request from within the same StreamHandle (under the hood posts to tool endpoint with stream context).
- resumeStream(stream_id, resume_token): returns new StreamHandle.

Ergonomic tradeoffs and rationale:
- Single event emitter style is familiar to JS devs; keeps surface tiny.
- Expose both raw and structured deltas to support clients that only want text (fast path) vs structured-aware UIs (full fidelity).
- Opted not to auto-merge structured patches into a canonical object because that creates heavy SDK state management; instead expose patches for apps to apply as necessary.

Backpressure and client-driven pacing:
- Server will prioritize latency SLO; but to avoid client overload, server may include a pacing hint header in checkpoint frames (e.g., recommended buffer_ms).
- SDK exposes buffer state and exposes a low-memory mode that asks server for larger but fewer frames.

Failure modes and recovery patterns:
- Transient disconnect: client can resume using resume_token before token TTL. If TTL expired, server returns EXPIRED_TOKEN and a re-run suggestion (idempotent prompt re-submit recommended).
- Partial tool response lost: server replays latest checkpoint and tool_event frames; clients rebind local UI via cid. If server cannot dedupe (cid not found), it will return tool_retry_needed with guided re-send path.

Telemetry and observability (what SDK collects):
- token_counts (per-checkpoint), chunk_latency_ms distribution, tool_call_latency_ms, resume_success/fail, socket_reconnect_count.
- Privacy note: SDK must not log prompt text to telemetry by default; only token counts and anonymized hashes.

Developer experience patterns and examples (notes to team):
- Example: editor assistant shows progressive suggestions as deltas. Tool-call path: model asks to call "code-runner" -> UI shows confirm button with small preview -> user clicks -> client callTool(cid, payload) -> SDK posts payload and streams tool_response back into same stream.
- Example resumed session: network hiccup -> client reconnects with resume_token -> receives resume_ack + last delta fragments to rehydrate UI.

Checklist for this sprint:
- [ ] API prototype for startStream + resumeStream (web socket + http fallback)
- [ ] Minimal Node + browser SDK with event emitter and callTool helper
- [ ] Server support for checkpoint/resume token and cid dedupe window
- [ ] Schema for structured_patch + small sample schemas for notes and actions
- [ ] Integration test harness: simulated disconnect, tool replays, resume TTL expiry
- [ ] Telemetry hooks and privacy review (security team)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Resume token format: opaque string vs compact vector (opaque preferred for now).
- Checkpoint frequency: time-based (every 3s) vs token-based (every n tokens). Tradeoffs: time is predictable for UI; tokens correlate to cost. Proposed default: hybrid (every 2.5s or 64 tokens, whichever comes first).
- Deduplication TTL for cids: 30s vs 5m. Short TTL cheaper but more fragile for slow tool runtimes. Start with 30s and monitor.
- How to surface partial tool results while tool still running (streaming tool responses)? Support tool_response frames that themselves can be deltas/patches.

Next steps and owners (short):
- Priya: spin up SDK skeleton and event API (this sprint).
- Ethan: prototype resume token implementation and server checkpoint hooks.
- Mina: draft telemetry bucket + privacy appendix and own review with security.
- Jonah: run integration tests and simulate disconnects; validate cid dedupe behavior.

Notes to self: keep contract intentionally limited. If we can cover ~85% of in-house use cases with these primitives, we can iterate on advanced features later. Save complex session merge and multi-device sync for follow-on.

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (stream contract brainstorm)
- Jira: JIRA-HOSTED-872 (resume + tooling epic)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/178 (initial SDK sketch)

(End of sprint notes)
